## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.

There are tonnes of graphics in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the `plot()` function we used last day) and add on packages like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

We can use the in-built data frame `cars` to play with plotting:

```{r}
head(cars)
```

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now with ggplot:

> I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot2") in my quarto document.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Did not work.

Every ggplot needs at least 3 things (called layers) to work:

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics**, or **aes** (how the columns of the data map to the plot)
- the **geometry**, or **geom** (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data = cars) + 
  aes(x = speed, y = dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, color = "red", se = F) +
  theme_classic() + 
  labs(x = "Speed (MPH)",
       y = "Stopping Distance (ft)",
       title = "Silly Plot of Stopping Distances")
```

We have to do a bit more work to start the plot, but we have exponentially more customization.

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)

myplot <- ggplot(genes) +
       aes(x = Condition1, y = Condition2, col = State) +
       geom_point() +
       scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "grey", "blue")) + 
       labs(x = "Control (No Drug)",
            y = "Drug Treatment",
            title = "Gene expression changes upon drug treatment",
            subtitle = "GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo")

myplot

```

```{r}
myplot + theme_bw()
```


> Q. How many genes are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

> Q. How many are "up" regulated?

```{r}
table(genes$State)

#or

sum(genes$State == "up")
```

> Q. What percent of genes are "down" regulated?

```{r}

down_gene_fraction <- round((sum(genes$State == "down")/nrow(genes)*100), digits = 2)

down_gene_fraction
```

> Q. What percent of genes are "up" regulated?

```{r}

up_gene_fraction <- round((sum(genes$State == "up")/nrow(genes)*100), digits = 2)

up_gene_fraction
```

We can install extra packages with `install.packages()` like themed ones for Spongebob or Star Wars and use **patchwork** to combine plots

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2 | p3) / p4
```

```{r}
myplot + 
  facet_wrap(~State)
```

## The GapMinder data

The gapminder dataset is rather famous socioeconomic dataset that has lots of stuff we can plot (try not to be sad thinking about the realities).

```{r}
# File location online
library(gapminder)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

> Q. How many data entries are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```


> Q. How many countries are in this dataset?


*Ojo*, have a look!

```{r}
head(gapminder)
```

Not that helpful when its alphabetical...

Let's use the `unique()` function to get how many unique countries there are.

```{r}
unique(gapminder$country)

length(unique(gapminder$country))
```

Let's try to plot it now! Hopefully it won't end up depressing!

```{r}
sadplot <- ggplot(gapminder) +
       aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp) +
       geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
       labs(x = "GDP Per Capita",
            y = "Life Expectancy",
            title = "Saddest plot",
            subtitle = "for real")

sadplot
```

Let's add some color... yay...

```{r}
sadplot + aes(col = continent)
```

Let's split the continents by faceting

```{r}
sadplot + 
  aes(col = continent) +
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```

Let's try Histograms and Boxplots

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill = continent) + 
  geom_histogram()
```

```{r}
sadBoxplot <- ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(x = lifeExp, continent, fill = continent) + 
  geom_boxplot()

sadBoxplot

```
